subject: medicine
title: Dementia and delirium: reversible and progressive

steps.tx: Ask about **recent memory loss** with repeated questions, misplaced items and getting lost on familiar routes. Map **daily function** across cooking, money, medicines and driving, because lost independence stages severity. Probe behaviour with apathy, disinhibition and night wandering, and screen **delirium clues** such as fluctuating attention, infection or new sedatives. Exclude reversible causes like low B12, thyroid failure, depression and pressure hydrocephalus, and always take a carer history with school, job and baseline ability. Note stepwise decline with strokes or snoring.
steps.say: Ask about recent memory loss with repeated questions and getting lost on familiar routes. Map daily function across cooking, money, medicines and driving because lost independence stages severity. Probe behaviour with apathy, disinhibition and night wandering. Screen for fluctuating attention, infection or new sedatives because delirium fluctuates while dementia progresses. Always interview the carer and record schooling, job and baseline ability, then exclude reversible causes and note stepwise vascular decline.

steps.tx: Perform **cognitive testing** with orientation, recall and clock drawing using MMSE or MoCA, scored against schooling and baseline. Apply the **delirium screen** with the confusion assessment method for acute onset, inattention and fluctuating course. Watch **gait and neurology** for apraxic shuffling with incontinence in pressure hydrocephalus, brisk reflexes in vascular disease, and parkinsonism with visual hallucinations in Lewy body disease. Check frontal release signs, nutrition with glossitis and anaemia, and the full drug list for anticholinergic burden. Test urine for infection, stop sedatives, and secure gas, fire and wandering safety.
steps.say: Test orientation, recall and clock drawing with MMSE or MoCA and score against schooling and baseline. Apply the confusion assessment method because acute onset with inattention and fluctuating course marks delirium. Watch gait for apraxic shuffling with incontinence because pressure hydrocephalus is treatable. Look for brisk reflexes in vascular disease and parkinsonism with visual hallucinations in Lewy body disease. You should review nutrition, the full drug list and urine for infection, then stop sedatives and secure home safety.

steps.tx: Use the bedside forms for **cognitive testing** with MMSE and MoCA orientation plus the clock drawing task shown on the left. Apply the **CAM delirium check** on the right for acute onset, inattention and fluctuating course. Treat inattention with a fluctuating course as delirium until proved otherwise, and record the baseline score for follow up. Practise clock drawing and the CAM questions together because exams often pair dementia staging with delirium exclusion.

steps.tx: Send **reversible screens** with B12, thyroid function and syphilis serology, plus a full drug review. Request **brain imaging** with CT for atrophy, infarcts and hydrocephalus, and MRI for hippocampal loss, white matter disease and Lewy changes. Consider lumbar puncture for pressure hydrocephalus tap response or prion proteins, and EEG for diffuse slowing in delirium or periodic complexes in prion disease. Match patterns to **Alzheimer pattern** with amnestic hippocampal loss, stepwise vascular disease, visual Lewy disease with parkinsonism, or fluctuating delirium by bedside criteria. Involve geriatrics for capacity planning.
steps.say: Send B12, thyroid function and syphilis serology because reversible causes must be excluded first. You should review the full drug list for sedative and anticholinergic precipitants. You should request CT for atrophy, infarcts and hydrocephalus, and MRI for hippocampal loss and white matter disease. Consider lumbar puncture and EEG when hydrocephalus, prion disease or delirium is suspected. Match the pattern to Alzheimer, vascular, Lewy body or delirium criteria, then involve geriatrics for capacity and placement planning.

steps.tx: Treat **delirium first** by correcting the cause with fluids, oxygen and infection care, reorienting the patient and stopping sedatives. Start **Alzheimer drugs** with donepezil and add memantine for moderate disease, while controlling pressure, statins and smoking for vascular protection. Refer tap responsive pressure hydrocephalus for shunting, and treat depression that mimics dementia. Build **carer support** with respite and day services, avoid sedation and restraints that worsen falls, stop unsafe driving through licensing review, and track cognition with carer burden and home safety.
